edge_explainer: The screen called CAPD cheap at 7.6x EV/EBIT with net cash. Both halves fail, and not in the way the intake expected. Net cash was already refuted in-module: the vendor netted $99.8M of listed junior-gold-miner shares against debt as if they were cash, exactly the pro-forma the company itself prints in its annual report; the audited position is net DEBT of $31.4-31.8M. The intake then feared the $66.0M securities mark was inflating EBIT. It is not - the annual report's segmental walk puts the gain below operating profit, so EBIT of $46.6M is clean of it. The real problem is what sits between EBIT and the shareholder: $11.2M of levies charged on revenue rather than profit (disclosed inside the tax line) and $15.4M of finance charges at roughly 11% blended, which together eat 57% of operating profit before income tax or minorities. Attributable earnings excluding the mark were $3.4M statutory, or $12.4M on the company's own adjusted basis, against a $303M market cap - 24x to 90x, not 7.6x. Separately, the price move is a junior-gold cycle round-trip, not a de-rate: up 60% into February 2026 alongside GDXJ up 136%, then down 35.6% since 2 March against GDXJ down 33.8%. Operating EBIT is actually anti-correlated to gold (down 21% over four years while gold rose 138%), but roughly 38% of the market cap is literally a three-stock junior-gold equity book carried at fair value through profit, and drilling demand is a lagged derivative of junior financing conditions - so the market is pricing 2027 while the revenue guide prints 2025's boom. Management added $11.6M of fresh cash to the equity raises of two investees during Q2-2026 while the sector fell 14%, having diluted holders 14.6% at roughly 106p in Q4-2025 rather than sell any of a book that had tripled; the same investees are also drilling and laboratory customers, a loop disclosed in the strategic report but quantified nowhere in the related-party note. Fair value comes out at about 101p against 99.7p live - no edge, fat left tail.
